newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil port strike to start March 5 - Operators.
newsitem.headline: Brazil port strike to start March 5 - Operators.

text.p: Paranagua port operators said they had failed to reach an agreement with dock workers at the key Brazil port and confirmed a 72-hour strike would begin at 1200 local (1500 GMT) on March 5.
"The strike has been confirmed. It is scheduled for tomorrow at midday until Saturday at midday," said Carlos Roberto Frisoli, vice president of the port operators union SINDOP.
A negotiator for the port operators had earlier said a strike was 90 percent likely.

Dock workers at Paranagua are demanding a 21 percent pay increase which they say they are owed from last year and on Monday offered to call off the strike if they received their wage rise immediately.

But port operators say they will not discuss the wage issue by itself and they want a wide-ranging review of all aspects of port operation which include productivity and an increase in the amount of shifts worked.
"They don't want to discuss the other measures," said Frisoli, saying this was the main sticking point in discussions between the two sides.
"The strike to my knowledge is limited to Paranagua on Wednesday but there is some talk it could spread to other ports on Thursday and Friday," said Frisoli.
